spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact proposal surface: real Profiler construction under Document-Policy: js-profiling, a policy-less srcdoc frame proving the NotAllowedError gate, and a real trace searched for the marker field against the proposal's six-value vocabulary.

interactive.rationale: Both buttons work: the srcdoc attempt surfaced the real NotAllowedError, and the sample button took a 105-sample trace and filled the vocabulary table from it.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises two questions answered by trying, which is exactly what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the no-policy failure path (run for real), coarser-than-requested sampleInterval, and the no-field-at-all vs empty-marker distinction.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus, the WICG markers PR and the self-profiling spec are all linked.

conformance.rationale: The suite's assertions are well-designed, but the /v153/js-self-profiling-markers/conformance/ ROUTE is served without the Document-Policy: js-profiling header (verified with curl), so 5 of 6 assertions fail there — including one whose stated premise is that the suite's own page carries the header. The demo pages DO get the header via routes/release-endpoints.ts; routes/conformance.ts only special-cases the v147 js-profiling feature. This is a server bug, not an assertion bug.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Live on this build: construction permitted on the page, NotAllowedError in the policy-less frame, 105 samples with no marker field (0/6 vocabulary seen) — all displayed honestly; the only console error is the deliberate, documented policy-violation message behind the button.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts fire per branch but with literal-true conditions, so a trace whose shape breaks (no samples at all) would not flag.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; check rows use AA-safe emerald/rose on light backgrounds.

accessibility.rationale: Buttons named, outputs aria-live, vocabulary table has scoped headers, 12/12 visible focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3; table scrolls in its wrapper.

openQuestions.title: Serve Document-Policy: js-profiling on this feature's /conformance/ route (server fix)
openQuestions.detail: curl -sI http://localhost:3000/v153/js-self-profiling-markers/conformance/ shows no document-policy header, while the demo pages under the feature folder get one from routes/release-endpoints.ts. routes/conformance.ts adds the header only for v147/js-profiling-in-dedicated-workers. Result: the feature's conformance route fails 5/6 assertions (profiler-construction-is-policy-gated first among them) purely because of the missing header, contradicting the suite's own premise. Add the v153 js-self-profiling-markers case to routes/conformance.ts — fix the serving, do NOT touch the assertions.

openQuestions.title: Note: the marker field itself is absent on this 153 build
openQuestions.detail: A real 105-sample trace carried no marker field at all (0/6 vocabulary values seen) on Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, and the page reports that honestly. When a build ships the field, re-run and refresh this critique so the vocabulary table shows live values.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. The page is exemplary — real gate, real negative path, real trace — and it exposed a genuine server defect: the feature's conformance route is missing the Document-Policy header its own suite depends on.
